menu.subtitle: Since the operation that revealed the alien egg, your judgment has been monitored. Professor Chen believes he can shape the creature through your answers. The question is when to stop.

final.noMutationText: No new threshold. The current form stabilizes.

stable.label: Stable
stable.summary: The mutation is normal. The creature can still live with what it is.

strained.label: Strained
strained.summary: The answers are already trying to optimize it. Continuing increases the pressure.

anomaly.label: Anomalies detected
anomaly.summary: The search for improvement has gone beyond healthy mutation.

critical.label: Critical degeneration
critical.summary: It is no longer being shaped: it is coming apart under our demands.

confirmQuit.title: Quit the protocol?
confirmQuit.text: Your current progress will be reset and you will return to the main menu.

confirmStop.title: Leave it as it is?
confirmStop.text: Chen insists: with a few more protocols, he could correct its limits and create an almost perfect being. Stopping now means accepting this imperfect creature.

lore.title: Operation Mirador
lore.text: Your unit entered a restricted zone to secure an object that fell from the sky. The reports mention a mineral egg, a saturated radio, and a light that froze the whole squad.

lore.title: Contact and Trauma
lore.text: When the egg opened, you touched it to pull it away from a wounded soldier. Your heartbeat synchronized with its pulse, then your memories of the operation fractured.

lore.title: Clinical Doubt
lore.text: Since your evacuation, you answer simple exams correctly, but your moral choices shift under stress. Chen needs to know whether trauma has biased your judgment before letting you near the creature.

lore.title: Chen Protocol
lore.text: The professor connects the egg to the bioelectric spectrogram. With each answer, some signals stabilize while others shift. Chen believes he can guide that orientation, without yet knowing what it will ask in return.

force.name: Gatebreaker
force.description: The creature mostly inherits protection, lockdown, and retaliation reflexes.

exploration.name: Mistwalker
exploration.description: The creature mostly inherits curiosity, the outside call, and the need to see beyond the lab.

conciliation.name: Bond Echo
conciliation.description: The creature mostly inherits attachment, appeasement, and the refusal to be alone.

intelligence.name: Clearcore
intelligence.description: The creature mostly inherits analysis, restraint, and the need to understand.

stable.title: Viable bond
stable.text: The creature keeps a readable form. It senses your hypotheses, but does not yet suffer them as orders.

specialized.title: Genome under strain
specialized.text: The creature takes a clear direction. Every answer from the soldier stabilizes one faculty and weakens the others.

unstable.title: Hypothesis made flesh
unstable.text: Anomalies appear. By trying to improve it again and again, the protocol taught it that it was never enough.

degenerate.title: Total confusion
degenerate.text: The protocol was pushed too far. The lesson is brutal: searching for the perfect being ends up destroying the living one.

stopEnding.title: You refuse perfection
stopEnding.text: Chen promised a better creature after the next test, then an even better one after that. You chose to stop before turning a life into an optimization project. The creature remains imperfect, therefore alive.

stable.title: You refuse perfection
stable.text: Chen promised a better creature after the next test, then an even better one after that. You chose to stop before turning a life into an optimization project. The creature remains imperfect, therefore alive.

strained.title: You stop before the fracture
strained.text: The pressure was already there: each test promised a fairer, stronger, more complete version. You interrupt the protocol before that demand becomes a wound. It will remain unfinished, and that is exactly what saves it.

anomaly.title: You stop the damage
anomaly.text: The anomalies do not vanish because you close the file. You pushed too far, then chose not to correct one harm with another. The creature will live with those traces, away from the project that caused them.

critical.title: You look at what remains
critical.text: The protocol has already crossed the line. Stopping now erases nothing, but at least refuses the final violence: continuing in the name of repair. This is no clean victory, only responsibility accepted at last.

stable.title: It survives our questions
stable.text: You reached the end without forcing it into one final form. Chen wanted a perfect conclusion; he gets a living being, readable but never finished. This is not a laboratory victory. It is a reprieve no one should mistake for a model.

strained.title: The protocol keeps its grip
strained.text: The creature still holds together, but its final form carries your insistence. Every improvement left a debt in its body. It is not destroyed, not perfect either: only constrained by the sum of our corrections.

anomaly.title: Improvement has marked it
anomaly.text: The anomalies are now part of its biological history. The protocol wanted to prove that a life could be optimized until it became acceptable. It mostly proves that by correcting endlessly, we teach a being it is never enough.

critical.title: Perfection won
critical.text: By searching for the ideal form, the protocol undid the one that existed. What remains is brutal: perfection does not save the living when it demands that life stop being imperfect.
